description: Bound the eager per-token logits/scores buffer the in-process embedder allocates but never reads. ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (grounded in source): LlamaCppEmbedder._load_model (src/kiro_crew/embeddings.py ~line 1327) constructs the vendored Llama with embedding=True, n_ctx=_N_CTX(2048), n_batch=_N_CTX(2048), n_ubatch=_N_UBATCH(512). The vendored Llama.__init__ (src/kiro_crew/_vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py lines ~476-478) eagerly allocates `self.scores = np.ndarray((n_ctx if logits_all==True else n_batch, self._n_vocab), dtype=np.single)`. The constructor's logits_all defaults to False, so the shape is (n_batch, n_vocab) = (2048, ~151000 for Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) which is ~1.24 GB of float32 allocated at model load. The embedding code path (Llama.embed / create_embedding) reads vectors via llama_get_embeddings_seq / llama_get_embeddings and NEVER reads self.scores, so this buffer is pure waste for an embedding-only model. It is a large baseline/startup allocation consistent with the reported ~600MB stable baseline climbing once the in-process embedding path is active (aligns with related issue #6216). Because embedding inputs are already clipped to _MAX_EMBED_CHARS (~6000 chars, well under 2048 tokens) and the physical micro-batch is _N_UBATCH(512), the logical n_batch does not need to be 2048 for correctness of last-token pooling on a single sequence. THE FIX: reduce the scores-buffer footprint for the embedder. Preferred approach: pass an explicit, smaller n_batch to the vendored Llama for the embedding model (e.g. align n_batch with _N_UBATCH so the scores array is (512, n_vocab) ~= 310 MB instead of 1.24 GB) OR make the scores allocation lazy/skip it when the caller does not need per-token logits. The coder must first CONFIRM which levers the vendored Llama.__init__ actually exposes (read llama.py around the scores allocation and the n_batch/n_ubatch/logits_all handling) and choose the change that (a) preserves byte-identical embeddings for inputs up to _MAX_EMBED_CHARS and (b) does not break the completion/logits path for any OTHER caller of the vendored Llama. If the vendored Llama is only ever constructed for embeddings within KiroCrew, a targeted constructor arg is safest; if it is shared, prefer changing only the embeddings.py construction call rather than the vendored default. Document the exact buffer-size math (n_vocab * chosen_n_batch * 4 bytes) in a code comment. Independent of FEAT-003.
steps: Read src/kiro_crew/_vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py lines ~85-100 (constructor signature incl. n_batch, n_ubatch, logits_all defaults), ~340-345 (self._logits_all assignment), and ~470-480 (self.input_ids / self.scores allocation). Confirm scores shape = (n_ctx if logits_all==True else n_batch, n_vocab) and that logits_all defaults to False at construction.

Confirm the embedding read path does NOT use self.scores: read Llama.embed / create_embedding (llama.py ~lines 1020-1185). Embeddings come from llama_get_embeddings_seq/llama_get_embeddings; kv_cache_clear()+reset() already run per call.

Determine n_vocab for the shipped model context and compute the current vs proposed scores allocation. Current: n_batch(2048) * n_vocab * 4 bytes. Proposed (n_batch=_N_UBATCH=512): 512 * n_vocab * 4 bytes. State the numbers (approx 1.24 GB -> 0.31 GB for a 151k vocab) in a comment.

Grep for all constructions of the vendored Llama class within src/kiro_crew (grep -rn 'Llama(' src/kiro_crew, and _load_llama_class in embeddings.py) to confirm whether KiroCrew constructs it anywhere other than the embedder. If the embedder is the only in-repo constructor, the change can be made at the embeddings.py call site with an explicit smaller n_batch.

Implement the fix in src/kiro_crew/embeddings.py LlamaCppEmbedder._load_model: pass an explicit n_batch aligned to _N_UBATCH (or introduce a dedicated _N_BATCH constant == _N_UBATCH) so the vendored scores buffer shrinks, keeping n_ubatch and n_ctx unchanged so accepted context and micro-batching are unchanged. Keep n_batch >= n_ubatch (llama.cpp requires n_batch >= n_ubatch) and >= the max tokens a single clipped embed input can produce (verify _MAX_EMBED_CHARS at ~4 chars/token stays within the chosen n_batch; if not, pick the smallest n_batch that safely covers a single clipped input for last-token pooling). Add a comment explaining the buffer-size rationale and that the embedding path never reads self.scores.

If (and only if) grep shows the vendored Llama is constructed solely for embeddings in this repo AND a smaller n_batch alone cannot fully avoid the waste, additionally consider guarding the self.scores allocation in the vendored llama.py to allocate lazily; if you touch the vendored file, keep the change minimal and clearly commented as a KiroCrew local patch, and ensure the completion/logprobs path (which does read self.scores when logits_all) still allocates correctly.

Add a unit test test/test_embed_scores_buffer.py that fakes the vendored Llama class (mirror the fakes in test/test_embeddings.py) to capture the kwargs LlamaCppEmbedder passes to the Llama constructor, and asserts n_batch is the reduced value (e.g. == _N_UBATCH) and n_ctx/n_ubatch are unchanged. If a real numpy is available in the fake, additionally assert the scores-buffer element count is bounded. The test must fail if the construction reverts to n_batch=n_ctx. Ensure the test runs under the pyenv 3.11.15 targeted harness from FEAT-001 (its own minimal conftest, -o addopts='').
acceptance_criteria: src/kiro_crew/embeddings.py constructs the embedding Llama with an n_batch strictly smaller than n_ctx (e.g. n_batch == _N_UBATCH), bounding the vendored scores buffer, with a comment stating the buffer-size math and that the embedding path never reads self.scores.
n_ctx and n_ubatch are unchanged so accepted context length and physical micro-batch (and therefore embedding vectors) are unchanged; n_batch >= n_ubatch is preserved.
New test test/test_embed_scores_buffer.py asserts the reduced n_batch is passed to the Llama constructor and would fail if the code reverted to n_batch == n_ctx.

`PYTHONPATH=src ~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python -m pytest test/test_embed_scores_buffer.py -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts='' -q` passes (using the FEAT-001 targeted harness; add a minimal local conftest if the root conftest blocks collection).
kiro_crew.embeddings still imports cleanly: `PYTHONPATH=src ~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python -c 'import kiro_crew.embeddings'` exits 0.
verification: Run the new test with the pyenv 3.11.15 targeted harness and confirm it passes and is meaningful (temporarily reverting the n_batch change should make it fail).
Show the diff of the construction call and the buffer-size comment; confirm n_ubatch and n_ctx are untouched.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Root cause confirmed against source, not just the plan.

--- Source confirmation ---
- src/kiro_crew/_vendor/llama_cpp/llama.py line ~477-479: self.scores = np.ndarray((n_ctx if logits_all == True else n_batch, self._n_vocab), dtype=np.single). Constructor logits_all default is False (signature ~line 92, self._logits_all assignment ~line 344), so the shape is (n_batch, n_vocab).
- The scores buffer is sized off the RAW n_batch constructor arg (line 478), which equals self.n_batch = min(n_ctx, n_batch) used everywhere else.
- Embedding read path (Llama.embed / create_embedding, llama.py ~1020-1185) returns vectors via llama_get_embeddings_seq / llama_get_embeddings and NEVER reads self.scores. The `logits_all = True` at ~line 1088 is a LOCAL flag for output marking inside embed(), unrelated to the constructor arg / scores shape. embed() already runs kv_cache_clear() per decode_batch, so per-call KV growth is bounded (that is not this bug).
- create_embedding() calls embed(..., truncate=True) (default), and embed() with truncate clips each input to n_batch tokens (line ~1145-1146) and raises ValueError if a single input still exceeds n_batch (~1152-1154). => n_batch is the per-input token ceiling, so lowering it below a real input's token count would truncate it and, under LAST-token pooling, change the vector.

--- Only in-repo constructor ---
`grep -rn 'Llama(' src/kiro_crew --include=*.py` (excluding _vendor) returns NOTHING; the vendored class is obtained only via _load_llama_class() (embeddings.py line 413) and constructed only in LlamaCppEmbedder._load_model (embeddings.py ~line 1345). So the fix is made purely at the embeddings.py call site; the vendored file was NOT touched (step 6 not needed).

--- The fix (src/kiro_crew/embeddings.py) ---
Added constant _N_BATCH = 1_536 next to _N_UBATCH, and changed the _load_model construction from n_batch=_N_CTX to n_batch=_N_BATCH. n_ctx (=_N_CTX=2048) and n_ubatch (=_N_UBATCH=512) are UNCHANGED, so accepted context, physical micro-batching, and therefore embedding vectors are unchanged. A block comment at the constant and an inline comment at the call site document the buffer math and that the embedding path never reads self.scores.

--- Why 1536 and not _N_UBATCH(512) ---
The plan's preferred 512 is NOT byte-identical-safe. Llama.embed(truncate=True) clips each input to n_batch tokens; inputs are clipped to _MAX_EMBED_CHARS (6,000) chars at the code's own conservative ~4 chars/token, i.e. up to ~1,500 tokens. Real inputs already reach this range: knowledge chunker CHUNK_TOKEN_SIZE+CHUNK_OVERLAP = 800+200 = ~1,000 tokens/chunk (src/kiro_crew/knowledge/chunker.py), episodic memories up to 2,000 chars (~500 tokens). n_batch=512 would truncate any chunk/memory beyond ~512 tokens and change its last-token-pooled vector. So n_batch must be >= ~1,500. 1,536 == 3 * _N_UBATCH is the smallest multiple of the micro-batch that clears 1,500, is strictly < _N_CTX (bounding the buffer), and keeps n_batch >= n_ubatch (llama.cpp requirement). Byte-identical for every input up to _MAX_EMBED_CHARS.

--- Buffer-size math (n_vocab = 151,936 for Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) ---
Old: 2048 * 151936 * 4 bytes = 1,244,987,392 B ~= 1.24 GB (1.16 GiB).
New: 1536 * 151936 * 4 bytes =   933,740,544 B ~= 0.93 GB (0.87 GiB).
Reclaimed ~= 311 MB (0.29 GiB) of float32 allocated once at model load and never read on the embedding path. (If a smaller vocab custom model is used the saving scales with n_vocab; the ratio is fixed at 1536/2048 = 0.75, i.e. a 25% cut of that buffer.)

--- New test: test/test_embed_scores_buffer.py ---
Self-contained (does not import test/test_embeddings.py), fakes the vendored Llama class the same way (records constructor kwargs, returns a fixed-width embedding for create_embedding), never loads a real model or hits the network. Four tests: (1) n_batch == _N_BATCH and n_batch < n_ctx; (2) n_ctx == _N_CTX and n_ubatch == _N_UBATCH; (3) n_batch >= _MAX_EMBED_CHARS//4 and n_batch >= n_ubatch; (4) emulated (n_batch,n_vocab) element count is < the old n_ctx-sized count and under 1 GiB.
